newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan potash firm 1996 profit up 21 pct.
newsitem.headline: Jordan potash firm 1996 profit up 21 pct.

text.p: Jordan's Arab Potash Company net profits rose 21 percent to 33.2 million dinars in 1996 despite only modest increases in sales and pre-tax profits.
A copy of the firm's shareholders' report obtained by Reuters on Thursday showed net profits in 1995 were 27.4 million dinars.
Pre-tax profits rose just two percent to 44.1 million dinars in 1996 from 43.2 million dinars in 1995, while sales rose by a similar margin to 131.27 million dinars from 128.32 million.
Jordan last year sharply cut corporate taxes, boosting the balance sheets of many companies despite largely uninspiring 1996 performances outside the banking sector.
Total assets of the potash company rose to 313.4 million dinars at end of 1996 from 296.7 million dinars at end of 1995.
Shareholders rights rose to 202.6 million dinars from 185.6 million dinars.
Jordan, one of the world's major producers of potash, a key ingredient in the fertiliser industry, is expected to benefit from the continued growth of its traditional Asian markets.
The company, a key public shareholding company, is 57 percent state-owned but several Arab states, including Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have minority holdings.
